Shardul Thakur Defends Shreyas Iyer Amid India's T20I Struggles Against New Zealand

Match Context and Result

India faced New Zealand in the fourth T20I of the ongoing series in Auckland on Friday. The hosts set a target of 260 runs. In response, India finished their innings at 172/9, resulting in an 87-run defeat for the visiting side.

Shardul Thakur's Analysis on Shreyas Iyer

Speaking during a review of the match on SonyLIV, Indian all-rounder Shardul Thakur addressed questions surrounding captain Shreyas Iyer's batting returns in the series. Thakur argued that middle-order players should not be judged hastily based on a small sample of performances.

  • Batting Position Challenges: Thakur explained that players batting at No. 4—or occasionally No. 5 depending on tactical left-handed promotions—cannot independently set the momentum of the innings.
  • Game Adaptation: Unlike top-order batters, middle-order players must react to the scoreboard and match situation immediately upon arrival, while also balancing the requirement to finish innings effectively.
  • Series Statistics: Iyer has accumulated 76 runs across the first four matches of the series at an average of 19, which includes a 42-run knock off 28 balls in the opening fixture and a 22-run contribution in Auckland.

Captaincy Responsibilities

According to Thakur, the added burden of leading the national side can influence a player's decision-making on the field. However, he referenced Iyer's previous leadership experience in domestic cricket and the Indian Premier League (IPL) as proof of his capability. Thakur noted that Iyer has reached the IPL final with multiple franchises, including a title victory with Kolkata Knight Riders and a runner-up finish with Punjab.

Thakur concluded that fluctuations are common in the shortest format of the game and urged observers not to draw definitive conclusions about players or captains based on short-term form.
